title: The 4th largest lake on Earth disappeared

beats.vo: This was the fourth largest lake on Earth.
beats.caption: The 4th largest lake on Earth

beats.vo: Watch it disappear in one lifetime.
beats.caption: Watch it disappear in one lifetime

beats.vo: 1960. Two rivers feed it. Then the rivers are diverted to grow cotton.
beats.caption: Two rivers feed it. Then they're diverted for cotton.

beats.vo: The water pulls back. Kilometre by kilometre.
Fishing towns end up one hundred kilometres from the shore.
beats.caption: Fishing towns end up 100 km from the shore

beats.vo: The seabed turns to salt. The wind carries it for hundreds of miles.
beats.caption: The seabed turns to salt

beats.vo: By 2014, the eastern basin is gone.
beats.caption: By 2014 the eastern basin is gone

beats.vo: Ninety percent of the water. Gone.
beats.caption: 90% of the water. Gone.

beats.vo: It took ten thousand years to fill. Fifty years to empty.
beats.caption: 10,000 years to fill. 50 years to empty.

beats.vo: Would you have stopped it? Comment yes or no.
beats.caption: Would you have stopped it? Yes or no

meta.description:
In 1960 the Aral Sea was the fourth largest lake on Earth. Its two rivers were diverted to irrigate cotton, and in one lifetime 90% of the water was gone, leaving a salt desert where fishing fleets once sailed.

Watch our planet change in seconds. Accelerated geographic shifts, urban growth and climate overviews from a clean satellite perspective.

📍 Aral Sea, Kazakhstan / Uzbekistan · 1960 → 2024
🎬 Stylized satellite reconstruction based on real-world change.

Would you have stopped it? 👇
